**F-A (BLOCKING — this is claim 6). § Breaking's consumer set omits `@orkestrel/brief` entirely and under-names `@orkestrel/workflow`; its closing sentence "No other consumer reads the discriminant" is false.**

What is wrong. The report's § Breaking derives the consumer set from two patterns: `readonly type\??:\s*'(string|number|…)'` and `\bshape\.type\b|ContractShape\['type'\]`. The second is case-sensitive and anchored on a lowercase `shape`, so it cannot match a discriminant read through an identifier whose noun is capitalised (`briefShape.type`, `taskShape.type`) or through a property chain (`bail.inner.type`). Running `[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\.type\b` over `/home/user/fleet/**/{src,tests}/**/*.ts` returns the sites the two narrow patterns missed:

- `/home/user/fleet/brief/tests/src/core/shapers.test.ts:304` — `expect(briefShape.type).toBe('object')`. `briefShape` is `objectShape(…)` at `/home/user/fleet/brief/src/core/shapers.ts:143`, so its static type is `ObjectShape`, a `ContractShape` member. `/home/user/fleet/brief/package.json:74` declares `"@orkestrel/contract": "^0.0.15"`. `@orkestrel/brief` appears in the unit brief's § Consumers list and appears nowhere in § Breaking — not as breaking, not as cleared.
- `/home/user/fleet/workflow/tests/src/core/shapers.test.ts` — § Breaking names `.type ===` at `:24, :35, :42, :54, :64, :79, :89, :111, :119` and misses twelve further discriminant reads at `:18` (`taskShape.type`), `:21` (`taskShape.properties.description.type`), `:23` (`behavior.type`), `:34` (`field.type`), `:49` (`phaseShape.properties.tasks.type === 'array'`), `:53` (`concurrency.type`), `:63` (`bail.type`), `:75` (`workflowShape.properties.phases.type === 'array'`), `:78` (`bail.type`), `:100` (`workflowShape.properties.id.type === 'string'`), `:105`, `:120` (`behavior.inner.type === 'string'`).

Why it matters. The unit brief's § Consumers fixes the obligation: "Record each consumer-side edit the row obliges as an exact patch under § Shared-file patches in your report; the Orchestrator carries it to that package's unit in layer order." A consumer absent from § Breaking gets no unit. `ObjectShape` declares no `type` member after the rename, so `@orkestrel/brief` reddens on `npm run check` the moment it re-pins — after `@orkestrel/contract` has already published, which is the exact failure the section exists to prevent. `@orkestrel/workflow` gets a unit, but one whose patch list closes only part of its own red set, so that unit reports green against an incomplete edit and its remaining twelve sites surface as its own defect.

What right looks like. Re-derive the consumer set with a pattern that reaches a capitalised noun and a property chain — `[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\.type\b` over `/home/user/fleet/**/{src,tests,app}/**/*.ts`, ruling each hit by the static type of the receiver rather than by the match — and record the ruling for every hit, including the cleared ones. Then add to § Breaking: an `@orkestrel/brief` entry naming `/home/user/fleet/brief/tests/src/core/shapers.test.ts:304` with the exact edit `expect(briefShape.category).toBe('object')`; and extend the `@orkestrel/workflow` entry with the twelve line numbers listed here, each `.type` becoming `.category`. State the cleared packages by the read that cleared them (`contract.schema.type` is a `JSONSchema` read; `ColumnSpec.type` and `ColumnSchema.type` are toolbox's and database's own members) rather than by the sentence "No other consumer reads the discriminant".
